Information received since the June meeting indicates continued labor-market strengthening and moderate growth, while 12-month inflation remains below the 2 percent objective. This mix supports a gradual, inertial policy path consistent with forward-looking Taylor-rule behavior (Clarida, Galí, and Gertler) and expectations management under symmetric inflation targeting (Svensson and Woodford, 2005). Low market-based inflation compensation points to anchored expectations, which justifies maintaining accommodation, using forward guidance, and beginning balance-sheet normalization rather than aggressive near-term hikes (Goodfriend, 2002; Bernanke and Mihov).
